name: Fidelity National Information Services, Inc.
executive_summary: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) screens as a strong buy on classic value metrics — trailing P/E ~7.8x, P/B ~1.3x, dividend yield ~4.2%, and ROE ~17% — against a recurring-revenue banking and capital-markets technology franchise. The investment case rests on a simplified post-Worldpay model, the January 2026 acquisition of Global Payments’ Issuer Solutions business, and mid-single-digit organic revenue growth with improving Banking margins. The central debate is whether headline cheapness survives materially higher leverage (~$16.9bn total debt post-deal), heavy goodwill/intangibles, and integration plus interest-cost drag. We see a credible value entry for patient investors, but earnings quality is currently distorted by one-offs and the balance sheet is no longer conservative.
investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen flags FIS with 13 of 22 models passing (composite score 94%), spanning cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk families — unusually broad for a technology name. That aligns with a business whose revenue is predominantly recurring (82% of Q1 2026 revenue per the March 2026 10-Q) and contractually underpinned (~$25.5bn of remaining performance obligations as of 31 March 2026).

For a value investor, the hook is a de-risked strategic pivot: FIS sold 55% of Worldpay in January 2024, exited its remaining 45% stake on 9 January 2026, and redeployed proceeds plus ~$7.7bn of new debt into Issuer Solutions — repositioning as a core banking, payments-issuer, and capital-markets platform provider rather than a merchant-acquiring conglomerate. Annual revenue from continuing operations rose from $9.83bn (2023) to $10.13bn (2024) and $10.68bn (2025) per the FY2025 10-K segment table — roughly 4% CAGR with Banking Solutions growing from $6.74bn to $7.29bn.

Interim filings confirm operational momentum into the deal close: nine-month 2025 revenue reached $7.87bn (+4% YoY), Banking Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 45.8% in Q3 2025 (from 45.2%), and Q1 2026 revenue of $3.30bn (+30% reported; +7% pro forma at $3.35bn vs $3.13bn) reflects Issuer Solutions contribution. The screen’s FCF yield and dividend-growth passes are supported by historically strong cash conversion — though 2025 free cash flow and full-year cash-flow statement detail are not available in the truncated 10-K body extracts and are cited from Yahoo below.

Business quality markers include Fortune 500/S&P 500 membership, FFIEC-supervised bank-technology provider status, and sticky multi-year processing contracts. At ~7x earnings and ~4% yield, the market appears to price execution risk from the Worldpay era and balance-sheet concerns rather than a broken franchise.
financial_review:
Primary source: SEC EDGAR filings (regime: sec_edgar). The index contains two annual 10-Ks (FY2024 filed February 2025; FY2025 filed February 2026), six interim 10-Qs (Q2 2024 through Q1 2026), and nine 8-Ks (seven without body extracts). Annual filing bodies are truncated at 80,000 characters and do not include Item 7 MD&A financial tables or Item 8 consolidated income/cash-flow statements; interim 10-Q bodies are more complete.

Annual revenue (10-K segment tables, continuing operations)
- 2025: $10,677m total ($7,285m Banking; $3,196m Capital Markets; $196m Corporate & Other)
- 2024: $10,127m ($6,892m; $2,979m; $256m)
- 2023: $9,831m ($6,743m; $2,766m; $322m)
Revenue growth accelerated modestly: +5.4% in 2025 vs +3.0% in 2024.

Annual profitability, cash flow, and year-end balance sheet (gap — Yahoo fallback)
Full-year net income, operating income, EBITDA, free cash flow, and complete balance-sheet lines are not present in the available 10-K body extracts. Per financials_annual.json (Yahoo, fetched 25 July 2026), continuing operations for 2025 show revenue $10,677m (consistent with filings), operating income $1,759m, net income $382m, EBITDA $3,450m, and free cash flow $1,827m. For 2024: revenue $10,127m (consistent), operating income $1,761m, net income from continuing operations $790m (total reported net income $1,450m including $663m discontinued Worldpay-related operations). Reported net income is not a clean earnings yardstick given Worldpay disposals, equity-method volatility, and 2026 one-offs.

Interim trends (10-Q filings)

Q1 2026 (filed 8 May 2026) — first quarter including Issuer Solutions (closed 9 January 2026):
- Revenue: $3,295m vs $2,532m (+30%); pro forma revenue $3,350m vs $3,130m (+7%)
- Operating income: $423m vs $347m; operating margin ~13%
- Reported net earnings: $2,366m ($4.58 diluted EPS), driven by a ~$2.2bn pre-tax gain on the Worldpay minority sale (equity-method investment earnings $2,214m)
- Pro forma net earnings attributable to FIS: $187m vs $2,201m (2025 pro forma adjusted for the Worldpay gain remeasurement)
- Operating cash flow: $713m vs $457m
- Issuer Solutions contributed $591m revenue and $35m income (9 January–31 March)

Q1 2025 (filed 6 May 2025):
- Revenue $2,532m (+3%); operating income $347m (14% margin)

Nine months ended 30 September 2025 (filed 5 November 2025):
- Revenue $7,865m vs $7,528m (+4%)
- Operating income $1,212m vs $1,215m (flat)
- Banking revenue $5,420m (+5%); Banking Adjusted EBITDA $2,345m (+2%); Q3 Banking Adjusted EBITDA margin 45.8%

Balance sheet and leverage (Q1 2026 10-Q)
- 31 March 2026: total assets $43.5bn; goodwill $24.6bn; total debt $16.9bn (vs $10.4bn at 31 December 2025); cash $755m; stockholders’ equity $16.0bn
- Weighted-average debt interest rate 4.2% (3.7% including net investment hedge effects)
- Commercial paper outstanding: $4.2bn; revolving credit capacity ~$2.7bn net of CP backstop (per Note 7)
- March 2026: $6.3bn senior notes issued; proceeds repaid the $7.7bn term facility used to fund Issuer Solutions and reduced CP
- Tangible book value is deeply negative once $29bn+ of goodwill and intangibles are deducted — a screen blind spot

Cash returns
Dividends: $0.44/share declared in Q1 2026 ($232m paid). Yahoo shows ~$847m dividends and ~$1.4bn buybacks in 2025 under the August 2024 $3.0bn repurchase programme (~$1.8bn remaining at 31 March 2026 per 10-Q).

Filing gaps
Annual income statements, cash-flow statements, covenant compliance detail, and pension footnotes are missing from truncated 10-K bodies. Q1 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA tables are also truncated. No going-concern language was identified in available extracts.
risks_and_flags:
Leverage and interest burden: Total debt rose ~63% in Q1 2026 to fund Issuer Solutions. The 10-Q states management expects “future cash paid for interest to increase from historic levels.” With ~$4.2bn in commercial paper and $17bn total debt, refinancing and rate sensitivity are material; covenant detail is not in the available 10-K extract.

Integration and goodwill: The Issuer Solutions purchase price was ~$13.5bn (enterprise value), adding ~$6.5bn goodwill and ~$3.6bn intangibles. Goodwill impairment was not triggered at 31 March 2026 (qualitative assessment), but $16m Corporate goodwill impairment was recorded in Q1. Purchase-price allocation remains provisional.

Worldpay legacy exposures: Through 31 December 2026, FIS maintains parental guarantees on Worldpay standby letters of credit ($288m capacity) and a CVR liability ($378m due October 2027). The company considers loss “remote” but indemnification complexity persists.

Litigation and governance: Securities class action over former Merchant Solutions disclosures reached settlement (expected substantially insurance-funded; preliminary approval February 2026; final hearing July 2026 per Q1 10-Q). Shareholder derivative demands and related actions (Hialeah, McCollum) remain active; the board rejected demands in November 2025 and moved to dismiss. News reports a $210m settlement approval (10 July 2026).

Regulatory intensity: FIS is an FFIEC-examined bank service provider, faces CFPB/SEC/FINRA oversight in multiple subsidiaries, and was designated a DORA Critical Provider in November 2025 — adding direct ESA supervision for EU financial-institution clients. April 2025 news flagged regulatory scrutiny of the name.

Earnings quality: Reported Q1 2026 EPS is not representative of run-rate economics. Equity-method Worldpay swings ($526m loss in FY2025 per Yahoo; $2.2bn gain in Q1 2026 per 10-Q) distort P/E-based screens.

Operational/transformation costs: Q1 2026 M&A integration ($55m) and enterprise transformation ($93m) totalled $148m in Corporate & Other; severance continues through 2026.

Competitive/cyclical: Filings warn of intense competition from global banks’ in-house tech, fintech disruptors, and pricing pressure on contract renewals; transaction volumes are economically sensitive.

Pension/employee benefits: Yahoo balance sheet shows non-current employee benefit/pension obligations (~$491m combined); detailed pension funding status is not in available 10-K extracts.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is adequate on strategy and corporate actions, though much recent flow is institutional trading commentary rather than fundamental breaks.

Material developments:
- 9 January 2026: Issuer Solutions acquisition and Worldpay minority sale closed (10-Q; AD HOC NEWS, 25 July 2026).
- 24 February 2026: FY2025 results and 2026 guidance issued (8-K).
- 10 March 2026: $6.3bn senior notes issued to term out acquisition debt (10-Q Note 7).
- 10 July 2026: Judge approves ~$210m investor lawsuit settlement (FL Times-Union).
- 8 July 2026: Frankfurt International Bank cloud banking win (Yahoo Finance).
- July 2026: FIS joins Anthropic Project Glasswing / Mythos 5 AI cybersecurity initiative (Yahoo Finance, 21–22 July 2026).
- 8 May 2025: Q1 2025 earnings beat on Banking growth (Yahoo Finance).
- 5 April 2025: Regulatory spotlight article (Yahoo Finance).
- 15 July 2026: Perpetual Ltd opens ~$95.4bn position (Quiver Quantitative).
- 24 July 2026: Truist maintains rating but lowers price target to $43 (GuruFocus) — sentiment remains cautious despite value arguments.

Macro context (colour only): US 10-year yield ~4.68% and policy proxy ~3.81% (macro_context.json) reinforce that a levered, rate-sensitive issuer merits discount, but also cap multiple expansion until deleveraging is visible.
research_rationale: Thin press on securities investigations adds no new filing facts but keeps litigation live; Q3 leverage, trimmed outlook and leadership turnover still weaken the strong buy case.

Operational momentum in Banking is intact, but guidance, capital allocation and leadership turnover raise execution risk versus the July memo.
